methods.name: Pv
methods.signature: Pv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the present value of an investment. The present value is the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now. For example, when you borrow money, the loan amount is the present value to the lender.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate per period. For example, if you obtain an automobile loan at a 10 percent annual interest rate and make monthly payments, your interest rate per month is 10%/12, or 0.83%. You would enter 10%/12, or 0.83%, or 0.0083, into the formula as the rate.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity. For example, if you get a four-year car loan and make monthly payments, your loan has 4*12 (or 48) periods. You would enter 48 into the formula for nper.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period and cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt includes principal and interest but no other fees or taxes. For example, the monthly payments on a $10,000, four-year car loan at 12 percent are $263.33. You would enter -263.33 into the formula as the pmt. If pmt is omitted, you must include the fv argument.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0). For example, if you want to save $50,000 to pay for a special project in 18 years, $50,000 is the future value. You could then make a conservative guess at an interest rate and determine how much you must save each month. If fv is omitted, you must include the pmt argument.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1; indicates when payments are due.

methods.signature: NPer(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the number of periods for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate per period.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period; it cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt contains principal and interest but no other fees or taxes.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pv - the present value, or the lump-sum amount that a series of future payments is worth right now.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance that you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0).

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1 and indicates when payments are due.

methods.name: Pmt
methods.signature: Pmt(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the payment for a loan based on constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate for the loan.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payments for the loan.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pv - the present value, or the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now; also known as the principal.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (zero), that is, the future value of a loan is 0.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 (zero) or 1; indicates when payments are due.

methods.name: Rate
methods.signature: Rate(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the interest rate per period of an annuity. Rate is calculated by iteration and can have zero or more solutions. If the successive results of Rate don't converge to within 0.0000001 after 20 iterations, Rate returns the #NUM! error value.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period and cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt includes principal and interest but no other fees or taxes. If pmt is omitted, you must include the fv argument.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pv - the present value—the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0).

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1; indicates when payments are due.

parameters.name: Arg6
parameters.description: Guess - your guess for what the rate will be.

methods.name: MIrr
methods.signature: MIrr(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the modified internal rate of return for a series of periodic cash flows. MIrr considers both the cost of the investment and the interest received on reinvestment of cash.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Values - an array or a reference to cells that contain numbers. These numbers represent a series of payments (negative values) and income (positive values) occurring at regular periods.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Finance_rate - the interest rate you pay on the money used in the cash flows.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Reinvest_rate - the interest rate you receive on the cash flows as you reinvest them.

methods.name: Irr
methods.signature: Irr(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the internal rate of return for a series of cash flows represented by the numbers in values. These cash flows don't have to be even, as they would be for an annuity. However, the cash flows must occur at regular intervals, such as monthly or annually. The internal rate of return is the interest rate received for an investment consisting of payments (negative values) and income (positive values) that occur at regular periods.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Values - an array or a reference to cells that contain numbers for which you want to calculate the internal rate of return.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Guess - a number that you guess is close to the result of Irr.

methods.name: Match
methods.signature: Match(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the relative position of an item in an array that matches a specified value in a specified order. Use Match instead of one of the Lookup functions when you need the position of an item in a range instead of the item itself.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value: the value that you use to find the value that you want in a table.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Lookup_array: a contiguous range of cells containing possible lookup values. Lookup_array must be an array or an array reference.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Match_type: the number -1, 0, or 1. Match_type specifies how Microsoft Excel matches lookup_value with values in lookup_array.

methods.name: Weekday
methods.signature: Weekday(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the day of the week corresponding to a date. The day is given as an integer, ranging from 1 (Sunday) to 7 (Saturday), by default.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Serial_number - a sequential number that represents the date of the day you are trying to find. Dates should be entered by using the DATE function, or as results of other formulas or functions. For example, use DATE(2008,5,23) for the 23rd day of May, 2008. Problems can occur if dates are entered as text.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Return_type - a number that determines the type of return value.

methods.name: Search
methods.signature: Search(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Search and SearchB locate one text string within a second text string, and return the number of the starting position of the first text string from the first character of the second text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Find_text - the text that you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Within_text - the text in which you want to search for find_text.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Start_num - the character number in within_text at which you want to start searching.

methods.name: Transpose
methods.signature: Transpose(Arg1 As Variant) As Variant
methods.description: Returns a vertical range of cells as a horizontal range, or vice versa. Transpose must be entered as an array formula in a range that has the same number of rows and columns, respectively, as an array has columns and rows. Use Transpose to shift the vertical and horizontal orientation of an array on a worksheet.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - an array or range of cells on a worksheet that you want to transpose. The transpose of an array is created by using the first row of the array as the first column of the new array, the second row of the array as the second column of the new array, and so on.

methods.name: Atan2
methods.signature: Atan2(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the arctangent, or inverse tangent, of the specified x- and y-coordinates. The arctangent is the angle from the x-axis to a line containing the origin (0, 0) and a point with coordinates (x_num, y_num). The angle is given in radians between -pi and pi, excluding -pi.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the point.

methods.name: Asin
methods.signature: Asin(Arg1 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the arcsine, or inverse sine, of a number. The arcsine is the angle whose sine is _Arg1_. The returned angle is given in radians in the range -pi/2 to pi/2.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The sine of the angle that you want; must be from -1 to 1.

methods.name: Acos
methods.signature: Acos(Arg1 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the arccosine, or inverse cosine, of a number. The arccosine is the angle whose cosine is _Arg1_. The returned angle is given in radians in the range 0 (zero) to pi.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The cosine of the angle you want, and must be from -1 to 1.

methods.name: Choose
methods.signature: Choose(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Uses _Arg1_ as the index to return a value from the list of value arguments.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Specifies which value argument is selected. _Arg1_ must be a number between 1 and 29, or a formula or reference to a cell containing a number between 1 and 29.

methods.name: HLookup
methods.signature: HLookup(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant, [Arg4 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Searches for a value in the top row of a table or an array of values, and then returns a value in the same column from a row that you specify in the table or array. Use HLookup when your comparison values are located in a row across the top of a table of data, and you want to look down a specified number of rows. Use VLookup when your comparison values are located in a column to the left of the data that you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value - the value to be found in the first row of the table. Lookup_value can be a value, a reference, or a text string.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Table_array - a table of information in which data is looked up. Use a reference to a range or a range name.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Row_index_num - the row number in table_array from which the matching value will be returned. A row_index_num of 1 returns the first row value in table_array, a row_index_num of 2 returns the second row value in table_array, and so on. If row_index_num is less than 1, HLookup returns the #VALUE! error value; if row_index_num is greater than the number of rows on table_array, HLookup returns the #REF! error value.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Range_lookup - a logical value that specifies whether you want HLookup to find an exact match or an approximate match. If True or omitted, an approximate match is returned. In other words, if an exact match is not found, the next largest value that is less than lookup_value is returned. If False, HLookup will find an exact match. If one is not found, the error value #N/A is returned.

methods.name: VLookup
methods.signature: VLookup(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant, [Arg4 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Searches for a value in the first column of a table array and returns a value in the same row from another column in the table array.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value - the value to search in the first column of the table array. Lookup_value can be a value or a reference. If lookup_value is smaller than the smallest value in the first column of table_array, VLookup returns the #N/A error value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Table_array - two or more columns of data. Use a reference to a range or a range name. The values in the first column of table_array are the values searched by lookup_value. These values can be text, numbers, or logical values. Uppercase and lowercase text are equivalent.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Col_index_num - the column number in table_array from which the matching value must be returned. A col_index_num of 1 returns the value in the first column in table_array; a col_index_num of 2 returns the value in the second column in table_array, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Range_lookup - a logical value that specifies whether you want the VLookup method to find an exact match or an approximate match.

methods.name: Log
methods.signature: Log(Arg1 As Double, [Arg2 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the logarithm of a number to the base that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the positive real number for which you want the logarithm.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Base - the base of the logarithm. If base is omitted, it is assumed to be 10.

methods.name: Proper
methods.signature: Proper(Arg1 As String) As String
methods.description: Capitalizes the first letter in a text string and any other letters in text that follow any character other than a letter. Converts all other letters to lowercase letters.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text - text enclosed in quotation marks, a formula that returns text, or a reference to a cell containing the text that you want to partially capitalize.

methods.name: Trim
methods.signature: Trim(Arg1 As String) As String
methods.description: Removes all spaces from text except for single spaces between words. Use Trim on text that you have received from another application that may have irregular spacing.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text - the text from which you want spaces removed.

methods.name: Replace
methods.signature: Replace(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As String) As String
methods.description: Replaces part of a text string, based on the number of characters that you specify, with a different text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text in which you want to replace some characters.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The position of the character in _Arg1_ that you want to replace with _Arg4_.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The number of characters in _Arg1_ that you want the Replace method to replace with _Arg4_.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Text that will replace characters in _Arg1_.

methods.name: Substitute
methods.signature: Substitute(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, Arg3 As String, [Arg4 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Substitutes new_text for old_text in a text string. Use Substitute when you want to replace specific text in a text string; use Replace when you want to replace any text that occurs in a specific location in a text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text - the text or the reference to a cell containing text for which you want to substitute characters.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Old_text - the text that you want to replace.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: New_text - the text that you want to replace old_text with.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Instance_num - specifies which occurrence of old_text you want to replace with new_text. If you specify instance_num, only that instance of old_text is replaced. Otherwise, every occurrence of old_text in text is changed to new_text.

methods.name: Find
methods.signature: Find(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Finds specific information on a worksheet.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The name of the worksheet.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The name of the range.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The name of an argument to refine the search.

methods.name: IsErr
methods.signature: IsErr(Arg1 As Variant) As Boolean
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to any error value except #N/A.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: IsText
methods.signature: IsText(Arg1 As Variant) As Boolean
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to text.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: IsNumber
methods.signature: IsNumber(Arg1 As Variant) As Boolean
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to a number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: Sln
methods.signature: Sln(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

methods.name: Syd
methods.signature: Syd(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum-of-years' digits depreciation of an asset for a specified period.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Per - the period and must use the same units as life.

methods.name: Ddb
methods.signature: Ddb(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for a specified period by using the double-declining balance method or some other method that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset). This value can be 0.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is being depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Period - the period for which you want to calculate the depreciation. Period must use the same units as life.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Factor - the rate at which the balance declines. If factor is omitted, it is assumed to be 2 (the double-declining balance method).

methods.name: Clean

parameters.description: Any worksheet information from which you want to remove nonprintable characters.

methods.name: MDeterm

methods.description: Returns the matrix determinant of an array.

parameters.name: Arg1

methods.name: MInverse
methods.signature: MInverse(Arg1 As Variant) As Variant
methods.description: Returns the inverse matrix for the matrix stored in an array.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - a numeric array with an equal number of rows and columns.

methods.name: MMult
methods.signature: MMult(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Variant
methods.description: Returns the matrix product of two arrays. The result is an array with the same number of rows as array1 and the same number of columns as array2.

methods.name: Ipmt

methods.description: Returns the interest payment for a given period for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.

methods.description: Returns the payment on the principal for a given period for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1 and indicates when payments are due.

methods.name: CountA

methods.description: Multiplies all the numbers given as arguments and returns the product.

methods.description: Returns the factorial of a number. The factorial of a number is equal to 1\2\3\...\ number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the nonnegative number that you want the factorial of. If number is not an integer, it is truncated.

parameters.name: Arg3

methods.name: Days360

methods.description: Returns the number of days between two dates based on a 360-day year (twelve 30-day months), which is used in some accounting calculations.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: A Boolean value that specifies whether to use the U.S. or European method in the calculation.

methods.name: Vdb
methods.signature: Vdb(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, Arg5 As Double, [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for any period that you specify, including partial periods, by using the double-declining balance method or some other method that you specify. Vdb stands for variable declining balance.

parameters.name: Arg1

parameters.name: Arg7

parameters.description: Data_array - an array of or reference to a set of values for which you want to count frequencies. If data_array contains no values, Frequency returns an array of zeros.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Bins_array - an array of or reference to intervals into which you want to group the values in data_array. If bins_array contains no values, Frequency returns the number of elements in data_array.

methods.name: ChiDist

methods.name: Combin

methods.description: Returns the number of combinations for a given number of items. Use Combin to determine the total possible number of groups for a given number of items.

methods.name: Confidence

methods.description: Returns a value that you can use to construct a confidence interval for a population mean.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the value to round.

methods.name: ExponDist
methods.signature: ExponDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the exponential distribution. Use ExponDist to model the time between events, such as how long an automated bank teller takes to deliver cash. For example, you can use ExponDist to determine the probability that the process takes at most 1 minute.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value of the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Lambda - the parameter value.

parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that indicates which form of the exponential function to provide. If cumulative is True, ExponDist returns the cumulative distribution function; if False, it returns the probability density function.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value at which to evaluate the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom1 - the numerator degrees of freedom.

parameters.description: Degrees_freedom2 - the denominator degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom1 - the numerator degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom2 - is the denominator degrees of freedom.

methods.name: Permut
methods.signature: Permut(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the number of permutations for a given number of objects that can be selected from number objects. A permutation is any set or subset of objects or events where internal order is significant. Permutations are different from combinations, for which the internal order is not significant. Use this function for lottery-style probability calculations.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - an integer that describes the number of objects.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Number_chosen - an integer that describes the number of objects in each permutation.

methods.name: Poisson
methods.signature: Poisson(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Poisson distribution. A common application of the Poisson distribution is predicting the number of events over a specific time, such as the number of cars arriving at a toll plaza in 1 minute.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the number of events.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the expected numeric value.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that determines the form of the probability distribution returned. If cumulative is True, Poisson returns the cumulative Poisson probability that the number of random events occurring will be between zero and x inclusive; if False, it returns the Poisson probability mass function that the number of events occurring will be exactly x.

methods.name: TDist
methods.signature: TDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Percentage Points (probability) for the Student t-distribution where a numeric value (x) is a calculated value of t for which the Percentage Points are to be computed. The t-distribution is used in the hypothesis testing of small sample data sets. Use this function in place of a table of critical values for the t-distribution.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the numeric value at which to evaluate the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom - an integer indicating the number of degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Tails - specifies the number of distribution tails to return. If tails = 1, TDist returns the one-tailed distribution. If tails = 2, TDist returns the two-tailed distribution.

methods.name: Weibull
methods.signature: Weibull(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Weibull distribution. Use this distribution in reliability analysis, such as calculating a device's mean time to failure.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value at which to evaluate the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Alpha - a parameter to the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Beta - a parameter to the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Cumulative - determines the form of the function.

methods.name: SumXMY2
methods.signature: SumXMY2(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of squares of differences of corresponding values in two arrays.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array_x - the first array or range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array_y - the second array or range of values.

methods.name: SumX2MY2
methods.signature: SumX2MY2(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of the difference of squares of corresponding values in two arrays.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array_x - the first array or range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array_y - the second array or range of values.

methods.name: SumX2PY2
methods.signature: SumX2PY2(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of the sum of squares of corresponding values in two arrays. The sum of the sum of squares is a common term in many statistical calculations.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array_x - the first array or range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array_y - the second array or range of values.

methods.name: ChiTest
methods.signature: ChiTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the test for independence.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The range of data that contains observations to test against expected values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The range of data that contains the ratio of the product of row totals and column totals to the grand total.

methods.name: Correl
methods.signature: Correl(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the correlation coefficient of the _Arg1_ and _Arg2_ cell ranges.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A cell range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: A second cell range of values.

methods.name: Covar
methods.signature: Covar(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns covariance, the average of the products of deviations for each data point pair.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The first cell range of integers.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The second cell range of integers.

methods.name: FTest
methods.signature: FTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the result of an F-test. An F-test returns the two-tailed probability that the variances in array1 and array2 are not significantly different. Use this function to determine whether two samples have different variances. For example, given test scores from public and private schools, you can test whether these schools have different levels of test score diversity.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array1 - the first array or range of data.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array2 - the second array or range of data.

methods.name: Intercept
methods.signature: Intercept(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the point at which a line will intersect the y-axis by using existing x-values and y-values. The intercept point is based on a best-fit regression line plotted through the known x-values and known y-values.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - the dependent set of observations or data.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - the independent set of observations or data.

methods.name: Pearson
methods.signature: Pearson(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient, r, a dimensionless index that ranges from -1.0 to 1.0 inclusive and reflects the extent of a linear relationship between two data sets.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array1 - a set of independent values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array2 - a set of dependent values.

methods.name: RSq
methods.signature: RSq(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the square of the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient through data points in known_y's and known_x's. For more information, see Pearson. The r-squared value can be interpreted as the proportion of the variance in y attributable to the variance in x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - an array or range of data points.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - an array or range of data points.

methods.name: StEyx
methods.signature: StEyx(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the standard error of the predicted y-value for each x in the regression. The standard error is a measure of the amount of error in the prediction of y for an individual x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - an array or range of dependent data points.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - an array or range of independent data points.

methods.name: Slope
methods.signature: Slope(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the slope of the linear regression line through data points in known_y's and known_x's. The slope is the vertical distance divided by the horizontal distance between any two points on the line, which is the rate of change along the regression line.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - an array or cell range of numeric dependent data points.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - the set of independent data points.

methods.name: TTest
methods.signature: TTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the probability associated with a Student's t-Test. Use TTest to determine whether two samples are likely to have come from the same two underlying populations that have the same mean.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array1 - the first data set.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array2 - the second data set.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Tails - specifies the number of distribution tails. If tails = 1, TTest uses the one-tailed distribution. If tails = 2, TTest uses the two-tailed distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Type - the kind of t-Test to perform.

methods.name: Prob
methods.signature: Prob(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the probability that values in a range are between two limits. If upper_limit is not supplied, returns the probability that values in x_range are equal to lower_limit.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X_range - the range of numeric values of x with which there are associated probabilities.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Prob_range - a set of probabilities associated with values in x_range.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Lower_limit - the lower bound on the value for which you want a probability.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Upper_limit - the optional upper bound on the value for which you want a probability.

methods.signature: DevSq(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of squares of deviations of data points from their sample mean.

methods.name: GeoMean
methods.signature: GeoMean(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the geometric mean of an array or range of positive data. For example, you can use GeoMean to calculate average growth rate given compound interest with variable rates.

methods.name: HarMean
methods.signature: HarMean(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the harmonic mean of a data set. The harmonic mean is the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of reciprocals.

methods.name: SumSq
methods.signature: SumSq(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of the squares of the arguments.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number1, number2... - 1 to 30 arguments for which you want the sum of the squares. You can also use a single array or a reference to an array instead of arguments separated by commas.

methods.name: Kurt
methods.signature: Kurt(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the kurtosis of a data set. Kurtosis characterizes the relative peakedness or flatness of a distribution compared with the normal distribution. Positive kurtosis indicates a relatively peaked distribution. Negative kurtosis indicates a relatively flat distribution.

methods.name: Skew
methods.signature: Skew(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the skewness of a distribution. Skewness characterizes the degree of asymmetry of a distribution around its mean.

methods.name: ZTest
methods.signature: ZTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the one-tailed probability-value of a z-test. For a given hypothesized population mean, ZTest returns the probability that the sample mean would be greater than the average of observations in the data set (_array_); that is, the observed sample mean.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: _Array_ is the array or range of data against which to test the hypothesized population mean.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The value to test.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: _Sigma_ is the population (known) standard deviation. If omitted, the sample standard deviation is used.

methods.name: Large
methods.signature: Large(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the k-th largest value in a data set. Use this function to select a value based on its relative standing. For example, you can use Large to return the highest, runner-up, or third-place score.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of data for which you want to determine the k-th largest value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: K - the position (from the largest) in the array or cell range of data to return.

methods.name: Small
methods.signature: Small(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the k-th smallest value in a data set. Use this function to return values with a particular relative standing in a data set.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - an array or range of numerical data for which you want to determine the k-th smallest value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: K - the position (from the smallest) in the array or range of data to return.

methods.name: Quartile
methods.signature: Quartile(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the quartile of a data set. Quartiles often are used in sales and survey data to divide populations into groups. For example, you can use Quartile to find the top 25 percent of incomes in a population.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or cell range of numeric values for which you want the quartile value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Quart - indicates which value to return.

methods.name: Percentile
methods.signature: Percentile(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the k-th percentile of values in a range. Use this function to establish a threshold of acceptance. For example, you can decide to examine candidates who score above the 90th percentile.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of data that defines relative standing.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: K - the percentile value in the range 0..1, inclusive.

methods.name: PercentRank
methods.signature: PercentRank(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the rank of a value in a data set as a percentage of the data set. This function can be used to evaluate the relative standing of a value within a data set. For example, you can use PercentRank to evaluate the standing of an aptitude test score among all scores for the test.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of data with numeric values that defines relative standing.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: X - the value for which you want to know the rank.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Significance - an optional value that identifies the number of significant digits for the returned percentage value. If omitted, PercentRank uses three digits (0.xxx).

methods.name: Mode
methods.signature: Mode(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the most frequently occurring, or repetitive, value in an array or range of data.

methods.name: TrimMean
methods.signature: TrimMean(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the mean of the interior of a data set. TrimMean calculates the mean taken by excluding a percentage of data points from the top and bottom tails of a data set. Use this function when you wish to exclude outlying data from your analysis.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of values to trim and average.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Percent - the fractional number of data points to exclude from the calculation. For example, if percent = 0.2, 4 points are trimmed from a data set of 20 points (20 x 0.2): 2 from the top and 2 from the bottom of the set.

methods.name: TInv
methods.signature: TInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the t-value of the Student's t-distribution as a function of the probability and the degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - the probability associated with the two-tailed Student's t-distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom - the number of degrees of freedom with which to characterize the distribution.

methods.name: Power
methods.signature: Power(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the result of a number raised to a power.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the base number. It can be any real number.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Power - the exponent to which the base number is raised.

methods.name: Radians
methods.signature: Radians(Arg1 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Converts degrees to radians.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Angle - an angle in degrees that you want to convert.

methods.name: Degrees
methods.signature: Degrees(Arg1 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Converts radians into degrees.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Angle - the angle in radians that you want to convert.

methods.description: Creates subtotals.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A number indicating the aggregation function to be used by the method.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The first Range object for which a subtotal is to be calculated.

methods.name: SumIf
methods.signature: SumIf(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Adds the cells specified by a given criteria.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Range - the range of cells that you want evaluated by criteria.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Criteria - the criteria in the form of a number, expression, or text that defines which cells will be added. For example, criteria can be expressed as 32, "32", ">32", or "apples".

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Sum_range - the actual cells to add if their corresponding cells in range match criteria. If sum_range is omitted, the cells in range are both evaluated by criteria and added if they match criteria.

methods.name: CountIf
methods.signature: CountIf(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Counts the number of cells within a range that meet the given criteria.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The range of cells from which you want to count cells.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The criteria in the form of a number, expression, cell reference, or text that defines which cells will be counted. For example, criteria can be expressed as 32, "32", ">32", "apples", or B4.

methods.name: CountBlank
methods.signature: CountBlank(Arg1 As Range) As Double
methods.description: Counts empty cells in a specified range of cells.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The range from which you want to count the blank cells.

methods.name: Ispmt
methods.signature: Ispmt(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the interest paid during a specific period of an investment. This function is provided for compatibility with Lotus 1-2-3.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate for the investment.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Per - the period for which you want to find the interest; must be between 1 and nper.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods for the investment.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Pv - the present value of the investment. For a loan, pv is the loan amount.

methods.name: Roman
methods.signature: Roman(Arg1 As Double, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts an arabic numeral to roman, as text.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the Arabic numeral that you want converted.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Form - a number specifying the type of roman numeral you want. The roman numeral style ranges from Classic to Simplified, becoming more concise as the value of form increases.

methods.name: Asc
methods.signature: Asc(Arg1 As String) As String
methods.description: For double-byte character set (DBCS) languages, changes full-width (double-byte) characters to half-width (single-byte) characters.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The text or a reference to a cell that contains the text that you want to change. If the text does not contain any full-width letters, the text is not changed.

methods.name: Dbcs
methods.signature: Dbcs(Arg1 As String) As String
methods.description: Converts half-width (single-byte) letters within a character string to full-width (double-byte) characters. The name of the function (and the characters that it converts) depends upon the language settings. Read/write String.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The text or a reference to a cell that contains the text that you want to change.

methods.name: Phonetic
methods.signature: Phonetic(Arg1 As Range) As String
methods.description: Extracts the phonetic (furigana) characters from a text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Reference - a text string or a reference to a single cell or a range of cells that contain a furigana text string.

methods.name: BahtText
methods.signature: BahtText(Arg1 As Double) As String
methods.description: Converts a number to Thai text and adds a suffix of Baht.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A number that you want to convert to text, or a reference to a cell containing a number, or a formula that evaluates to a number.

methods.description: This method connects to a source to receive real-time data (RTD).

parameters.name: progID
parameters.description: A string representing the real-time server programmatic identifier.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: A server name, Null string, or vbNullString constant.

parameters.name: topic1
parameters.description: A String representing a topic.

methods.name: Hex2Bin
methods.signature: Hex2Bin(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts a hexadecimal number to binary.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the hexadecimal number that you want to convert. Number cannot contain more than 10 characters. The most significant bit of number is the sign bit (40th bit from the right). The remaining 9 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Places - the number of characters to use. If places is omitted, Hex2Bin uses the minimum number of characters necessary. Places is useful for padding the return value with leading 0s (zeros).

methods.name: Hex2Dec
methods.signature: Hex2Dec(Arg1 As Variant) As String
methods.description: Converts a hexadecimal number to decimal.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the hexadecimal number that you want to convert. Number cannot contain more than 10 characters (40 bits). The most significant bit of number is the sign bit. The remaining 39 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

methods.name: Hex2Oct
methods.signature: Hex2Oct(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts a hexadecimal number to octal.

parameters.name: Arg1

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Timeline: the independent array or range of dates or numeric data. The values in the timeline must have a consistent step between them and can't be zero. See Remarks.

parameters.description: Aggregation: Although the timeline requires a constant step between data points, Forecast_ETS aggregates multiple points that have the same time stamp. See Remarks.
